title: The oldest species of Serolidae (Isopoda: Sphaeromatidea: Seroloidea) from the early Miocene (Burdigalian) of Argentina
content:
Abstract
A new genus and species of Serolidae, Mioserolis feldmanni, from the Miocene of southern Argentina is the first confirmed occurrence of that family from the fossil record. The enclosing Quién Sabe Member of the Estancia 25 de Mayo Formation has been dated to early Burdigalian based upon zircon U-Pb dating. The specimen was likely preserved in a hyperpycnal ash flow in shallow marine settings and its morphology is remarkably similar to modern serolid isopods, the diversity of which is currently highest in the South Atlantic and the Southern oceans. The new species supports the hypothesis that modern biogeographic provinces were already in place by 10 million years ago.
